question: Could you analyze our data and identify which ten-year period starting from any movie release year present in the data had the largest number of films, considering consecutive ten-year periods beginning at each unique year? Only output the start year and the total count for that specific period.
sql:
SELECT starts.start_year, COUNT(m.MID) as film_count
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) as start_year
    FROM Movie
    WHERE TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) IS NOT NULL
) as starts
LEFT JOIN Movie m ON TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(m.year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) >= starts.start_year 
    AND TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(m.year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) < starts.start_year + 10
GROUP BY starts.start_year
ORDER BY film_count DESC, starts.start_year ASC

-- For each unique starting year, count films in the 10-year period [start_year, start_year+9]
WITH parsed AS (
    SELECT TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) as movie_year
    FROM Movie
    WHERE TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(year, ' ', -1) AS INTEGER) IS NOT NULL
),
start_years AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT movie_year as start_year
    FROM parsed
),
period_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        s.start_year,
        COUNT(p.movie_year) as film_count
    FROM start_years s
    LEFT JOIN parsed p ON p.movie_year >= s.start_year AND p.movie_year < s.start_year + 10
    GROUP BY s.start_year
)
SELECT start_year, film_count
FROM period_counts
ORDER BY film_count DESC, start_year ASC
LIMIT 10
